d: Israel’s Arab parties could hold the key to the country’s next government. After record voter turnout, they are projected to win 19 seats in the 120-member Knesset. Neither Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc nor the opposition has enough seats to govern alone. On paper, the numbers give the opposition a possible path to power - if it can secure Arab party support. So, can Israel’s Arab parties turn their electoral gains into political power? Or will longstanding political taboos keep them out of government? Palki Sharma tells you.
